summary: Henry Harkness was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as secretary at the College of Fort St. George until 1834 and was Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from 1834 to 1837.

Henry Hart Milman worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Eton College and Brasenose College under Horace Hayman Wilson, and served as Professor of Poetry at the University of Oxford from 1821 to 1831.

Henry Heras was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Col·legi del Sagrat Cor. He taught at Colegio del Salvador, became a Professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai in 1923, and founded the Heras Institute in 1926.

Henry Herbert Dodwell worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908-1922) and was a professor at SOAS from 1922 to 1946.

Linguist and Indologist Henry Hoenigswald completed his PhD at the University of Florence under Giacomo Devoto after studies in Munich, Zurich, and Padua. He taught at Yale and Hartford Seminary before serving as Associate Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1948-1985).

Henry Hughes Presler was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at North Dakota State University, Boston University, and the University of Chicago. He worked as a missionary (1937-1972) and held a post at Leonard Theological College (~1947-1972).

Henry James Sumner Maine was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar educated at Christ's Hospital and Pembroke College, Cambridge. He held professorships at Cambridge and Oxford, served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta, and was Master of Trinity Hall.

Henry Lee Shuttleworth worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. After studying at Pembroke College, Oxford, and the University of Cambridge, he served as Additional Lecturer (attested 1910) and Lecturer in Tibetan (1936-1948) at SOAS University of London.
Henry Martyn was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School, St John's College (~1797-1802), and studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist (~1804-1805).
Henry Miers Elliot was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Winchester College (~1820-1826) and served as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

Henry Morris worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Rugby School and the East India Company College (1846-1848), later serving as Judge of Godavery in the Madras Civil Service from 1848 to 1875.

Henry Nelson Wright worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied classics at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1888-1892), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1892-1925), and founded the Numismatic Society of India in 1910.

Henry Octavius Coxe worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Westminster School and Worcester College, Oxford, and held posts at the British Museum (1833-1838) and as Librarian at the Bodleian Library (1839-1881).

Henry Pitts Forster was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He joined the East India Company and Bengal Civil Service in 1783, later serving as Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, from 1803 to 1804.

Henry R. Hoisington was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Williams College and Auburn Theological Seminary. He served with the American Ceylon Mission (~1833-1849) and worked as instructor and principal at Batticotta Seminary.
Henry Rawlinson was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Director in 1862 and President from 1878 to 1881 of the Royal Asiatic Society.
Henry Rice was an Indology scholar who served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (~1869-1880) and for the Church of Scotland (1880-1905).

Henry Snyder Gehman studied at Franklin & Marshall College, the University of Pennsylvania, Dropsie College, and Episcopal Divinity School. Active in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, he taught at Princeton University and was Professor of O.T. at Princeton Theological Seminary.
Henry Steel Olcott was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He attended Columbia University from circa 1847 to 1849 and founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.

Henry Sullivan Jarrett, who studied at Prior Park College, worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served at the Board of Examiners, Fort William (1870-1894), and was Assistant Secretary in the Government of India's Legislative Department (~1870-1892).
